resources.string: Choose the computer UpNext runs on.
Looking on this network. UpNext shows up here while it runs with Allow other devices on (Settings › Devices and API).
Tap a computer to ask it to allow this device.
Tap Find a computer to choose yours from the computers on this network that run UpNext with Allow other devices on (Settings › Devices and API). Ones chosen before show up here by themselves.
If it\'s on this network, find it again with Find a computer, or allow Nearby devices for UpNext in Android\'s settings.
allowed before, not seen on this network now
Scan the QR code in UpNext\'s Settings › Devices and API, Add a device.
For a computer this network can\'t see, such as one on Tailscale.
That isn\'t an address. Try den.lan, 192.168.0.42:8787 or a full https:// address.
That isn\'t an UpNext QR code. Open Settings › Devices and API on the computer and choose Add a device.
Away from home, this network can\'t see the computer: use Add by address, or scan the QR code from Settings › Devices and API.
%1$s no longer allows this device. Ask it again.
Another UpNext answers at %2$s now, so this device didn\'t open it. If %1$s moved, it shows up here again when it is found on the network.
This device stops using UpNext on %1$s. It asks %1$s to remove it from its devices too, when it can reach it.
Forgotten here. %1$s still lists this device: remove it in Settings › Devices and API there.
On %1$s, UpNext shows that %2$s wants to use it. Check it shows %3$s, then tap Allow there.
Nobody answered in time. Ask again, then tap Allow on the computer.
On the computer, Settings › Devices and API, Add a device shows a six-digit code.

This device\'s keystore couldn\'t keep the token safely, so it wasn\'t saved. The computer lists this device already: remove it there in Settings › Devices and API, then restart this device and try again. Until then, open UpNext in the browser.

%1$s can\'t be opened at %2$s, where it was last opened: nothing answers there, or another UpNext does. An UpNext with its id answers at %3$s. Anyone on this network could copy that id, so use the new address only if you expect %1$s there (it changed networks, or the router gave it a new address).
the UpNext at the new address doesn\'t allow this device
Start the game on %1$s: a phone can\'t open the game\'s launcher.
No app on this device opens web links.
That link couldn\'t be opened on this device.
